definitions.explanation: Describes something that doesn't work, is broken, or is of poor quality. Also used when efforts fail.
Used to express prohibition or that something shouldn't be done. Very direct way to say 'no' or 'you can't do that.'

examples.japanese: ここで{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}ってはだめです。
examples.english: You're not allowed to take photos here.

examples.japanese: このパソコンはもうだめです。
examples.english: This computer is no good anymore.

examples.japanese: この{靴|くつ}はもうだめだから、{新|あたら}しいのを{買|か}います。
examples.english: These shoes are worn out, so I'll buy new ones.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}やってもだめでした。
examples.english: No matter how many times I tried, it didn't work.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}は{泳|およ}ぐのがだめです。
ここで{食|た}べてはだめですよ。
examples.english: You're not allowed to eat here.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}だけで{外|そと}に{出|で}てはだめだと{言|い}われています。
examples.english: We've been told that children are not allowed to go outside alone.

notes: A very useful and common word. The kanji form {駄目|だめ} exists but hiragana is more common. ~てはだめ/~ちゃだめ is a common pattern to express prohibition (similar to ~てはいけない). When something fails, だめだった means 'it didn't work out.'
